movement_source: row 'Cost to income ratio', column FY24 -> column FY25
headline: NAB's cash cost-to-income ratio (CTI) increased by 80 bps to 47.3% in FY25 from 46.5% in FY24. The movement was driven by operating expense growth of 4.6%, which outpaced the implied operating income growth. A significant portion of this expense increase ($130 million) was attributable to payroll review and remediation costs.

drivers.narrative: Total operating expenses rose $435 million or 4.6% to $9,848 million (ev-3). Excluding $130 million for payroll review and remediation, underlying expenses grew only 3.2% (ev-4). This expense growth contributed positively to the rising CTI.
Implied operating income growth was lower than expense growth, contributing negatively to the CTI movement. Specific income drivers are not quantified in the provided evidence records.

notable_items: Payroll review and remediation costs ($130 million)
limitations: Quantified driver contributions (ppt) are not provided because the specific operating income level for FY24 is not available in the evidence records to calculate the exact jaws split.
The narrative relies on the bank's stated expense growth rates rather than a full walk chart.
